questions.text: "All suspects ___ be presumed innocent until proven guilty." (strong legal principle)
questions.hint: "Must" = strong legal obligation

questions.text: "Defendants ___ ___ a lawyer — this right cannot be waived without full understanding." (= have the right to)
questions.hint: "Are entitled to + noun/infinitive" = have the legal right to

questions.text: "Witnesses ___ answer questions that might incriminate themselves." (no obligation)
questions.hint: "Don't have to" = no obligation — they may remain silent

questions.text: "Police ___ ___ entering private property without a valid search warrant." (formal prohibition)
questions.hint: "Are prohibited from + gerund" = formal legal prohibition

questions.text: "All companies ___ ___ annual reports to the financial regulator." (external obligation)
questions.hint: "Are required to + infinitive" = formal external legal obligation

questions.text: "Suspects ___ ___ of their rights as soon as they are detained." (must — passive)
questions.hint: "Must be + pp" = mandatory passive obligation

questions.text: "In the statute: all hearings ___ ___ recorded and archived." (formal legal document)
questions.hint: "Shall be + pp" = mandatory passive in written law

questions.text: "Evidence ___ ___ obtained through coercion — all such evidence must be excluded." (formal prohibition)
questions.hint: All three (must not be / may not be / shall not be) can express formal passive prohibition

questions.text: "The judge ___ ___ himself — he had a financial interest in the outcome." (= should have but didn't)
questions.hint: "Should have + pp" = past obligation not fulfilled

questions.text: "States ___ ___ credible human rights violations reported within their jurisdiction." (duty — obliged)
questions.hint: "Are obliged to + infinitive" = have a legal/moral duty to

questions.text: What is the "rule of law"?
opts: The principle that judges make all laws
Law applies equally to everyone, including the government; no one is above the law
Citizens must obey all laws without question
Courts have unlimited power over the executive
questions.correct: Law applies equally to everyone, including the government; no one is above the law
questions.hint: Reading 1: definition of rule of law

questions.text: "All parties ___ ___ access to full disclosure of evidence before the trial begins." (= have the right to)
questions.hint: "Are entitled to" = have the legal right to

questions.text: "Lawyers ___ ___ client confidentiality — breaching it is a serious professional offence." (obligation)
questions.hint: "Must maintain" = strong professional obligation

questions.text: "Juvenile defendants ___ ___ treated in the same way as adult defendants." (= it is forbidden to do this)
questions.correct: must not be / may not be
questions.hint: "Must not be + pp" = prohibition — this cannot be done

questions.text: What is "restorative justice"?
opts: A harsher form of punishment for serious crimes
A model focused on repairing harm and relationships rather than punishment
Compensation paid by the state to crime victims
A fast-track court process for minor offences
questions.correct: A model focused on repairing harm and relationships rather than punishment
questions.hint: Listening 3B: Dr. Mwangi's lecture

questions.text: "The sentence ___ ___ to a higher court within 28 days of the original ruling." (= is permitted to be)
questions.hint: "May be + pp" = passive permission

questions.text: "Diplomatic personnel ___ ___ local prosecution under international law." (= officially excused from)
questions.hint: "Are exempt from + noun/gerund" = officially excused from obligation

questions.text: Which expresses a recommendation, not a strict obligation?
opts: "Courts must be independent of political influence."
questions.hint: "Should" = recommendation — softer than "must" or "shall"

questions.text: What is "progressive realisation" in human rights law?
opts: Rights that expand over time to include new groups
The idea that economic rights must be fulfilled immediately and completely
States must make demonstrable progress towards economic rights using maximum available resources
Rights that are only applicable in progressive political systems
questions.correct: States must make demonstrable progress towards economic rights using maximum available resources
questions.hint: Reading 2: "progressive realisation"

questions.text: "Workers ___ ___ adequate compensation for unfair dismissal under employment law." (= have the right to)
questions.hint: "Are entitled to + noun" = have the legal right to

questions.text: "Police ___ ___ private property without a valid search warrant in all circumstances." (formal passive prohibition)
opts: all of the above are correct
questions.correct: all of the above are correct
questions.hint: All three are correct formal prohibitions — "all of the above"

questions.text: A formal accusation that a person has committed a serious crime is called an ___.
questions.hint: Listening 3: "under indictment"

questions.text: "The company was bound ___ comply with the terms of the agreement." (be bound to)
questions.hint: "Be bound to + infinitive" = legally committed to do something

questions.text: "Shall" in a legal document expresses the same meaning as "may."
questions.hint: "Shall" = mandatory obligation; "may" = permission

questions.text: What does "inalienable" mean in the context of human rights?
opts: Applying only to citizens of democratic states
Cannot be permanently taken away or given up
Subject to change by democratic vote
questions.correct: Cannot be permanently taken away or given up
questions.hint: Reading 2: "inalienable — cannot be permanently surrendered"
